_note: Curated list for the chemistry search (Milestone 3). Every detection and number comes from the paper listed with it; nothing is estimated. 'percent_of_h2o' = ice amount as a percentage of the water ice along the same line of sight (a range where the paper gives one). Coordinates: J2000/ICRS from the paper, or converted from its galactic/B1950 values (noted in coords_source). Entries with 'resolve' instead of ra/dec are looked up by name with the data server (SIMBAD). Compiled 2026-11-15.

h2o_ice.label: Water ice
h2o_ice.why: Water frozen onto dust grains. New planets can inherit it: the likely source of much of the water on worlds like Earth.

co2_ice.label: Carbon dioxide ice
co2_ice.why: Frozen CO₂ forms together with water ice; a store of carbon and oxygen.

co_ice.label: Carbon monoxide ice
co_ice.why: Freezes out only in the coldest, densest places; hydrogen atoms turn it into methanol.

ch3oh_ice.label: Methanol ice
ch3oh_ice.why: The simplest complex organic molecule. A starting point for bigger organic molecules; its bands are too weak for SPHEREx, so detections here come from other telescopes.

pah.label: PAH carbon molecules
pah.why: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons: flat, soot-like carbon molecules that glow when lit by ultraviolet starlight.

aliphatic.label: Chain-like organics (C–H)
aliphatic.why: Carbon chains with hydrogen attached (aliphatic C–H bonds): another form of organic carbon in space.

prelife.label: Signs of pre-life chemistry
prelife.explain: Places where the raw ingredients of life's chemistry have been seen together: water ice plus organic carbon (methanol ice, PAHs or chain-like organics). These are ingredients, not signs of life.

typical._note: Median ice amounts in % of water ice from the Spitzer ice legacy survey (Öberg et al. 2011, ApJ 740, 109, Table 2), for comparison.

targets.name: DR 21 (Cygnus X)
targets.coords_source: Spectrum position l = 81.6629°, b = +0.5502° in Hora et al. 2026, converted to J2000
targets.summary: SPHEREx mapped a ridge of water ice across DR 21, with CO₂ and CO ice absorption too.

references.label: Hora et al. 2026, ApJ (SPHEREx ice and PAH maps)

targets.name: LDN 935 “Gulf of Mexico”
targets.where: North America / Pelican Nebula complex, Cygnus
targets.coords_source: Field centre l ≈ 84.8°, b ≈ −1.2° in Hora et al. 2026, converted to J2000 (approximate centre)
targets.summary: SPHEREx measured water and CO₂ ice towards 231 stars behind this cloud; in some spots CO₂ ice is stronger than water ice.

references.label: Hora et al. 2026, ApJ (SPHEREx ice and PAH maps)

targets.name: NIR38 (Chamaeleon I)
targets.where: Chamaeleon I cloud, about 500 light-years away
targets.summary: JWST's Ice Age study found the coldest pristine ices yet: water, CO₂, CO, ammonia, methane and methanol, before any star warms them.

targets.name: J110621 (Chamaeleon I)
targets.where: Chamaeleon I cloud, about 500 light-years away
targets.summary: The second Ice Age sightline, even more hidden (about 95 magnitudes of dimming in visible light); the same ice inventory including methanol.

targets.name: Elias 16 (Taurus)
targets.where: Taurus dark cloud, about 450 light-years away
targets.summary: The classic test case for quiet-cloud ice: a background giant star seen through the Taurus cloud.

targets.name: W33A
targets.summary: One of the best-studied ice sources: deep water ice, CO₂, CO, ammonia and plenty of methanol.

targets.name: RAFGL 7009S
targets.coords_source: B1950 position in Zavagno et al. 2002, precessed to J2000
targets.summary: Methanol is the second most common ice here, about 30% of the water ice: among the highest known.

targets.name: NGC 7538 IRS 9
targets.summary: Ice that hasn't been warmed much yet, with a lot of CO₂ and CO and some methanol.

references.label: Gibb et al. 2000 compilation, via Garrod et al. 2008 Table 5
Boogert et al. 2004, ApJ (CH₄ and CH₃OH in IRS 9)

targets.name: Elias 29 (ρ Ophiuchi)
targets.where: ρ Ophiuchi cloud, about 500 light-years away
targets.summary: The brightest young star in the ρ Ophiuchi cloud; its ices are still cold and barely processed.

targets.name: HH 46 IRS
targets.summary: A low-mass young star with water, CO₂, CO and methanol ices.

targets.name: Orion Bar
targets.coords_source: JWST PDRs4All NIRSpec mosaic centre (Berné et al. 2022)
targets.summary: The textbook place where ultraviolet light from hot stars makes carbon molecules glow at 3.3 µm (PAH) and 3.4 µm (chain-like organics).

targets.name: M82 (Cigar Galaxy)
targets.where: Ursa Major, about 12 million light-years away
targets.summary: A whole galaxy where AKARI saw water and CO₂ ice near the centre and PAH and chain-like organics out into its galactic wind.

references.label: Yamagishi et al. 2013, ApJL (ices in M82)
